questions.question: The cap of a classic BIC ballpoint pen has a small hole at its tip. It isn't there to help the ink. What is it for?
questions.explanation: If someone swallows the cap and it lodges in their throat, air can still pass through the hole. It is a tiny design detail meant to save lives.

questions.question: The world's most famous restaurant star ratings are awarded by a guide that was launched in 1900 to sell which product?
questions.explanation: The Michelin brothers gave the guide away free to French motorists, hoping that more driving would wear out more tyres.

questions.question: Every summer, the Eiffel Tower measurably grows, by as much as 15 centimetres. What causes this seasonal growth spurt?
questions.explanation: The tower's wrought iron expands in summer heat and contracts again in winter, so its official height quietly changes with the seasons — the sun-facing side even expands more, making the top lean slightly away from the sun.

questions.question: From the ground a rainbow always looks like an arch, but pilots flying above the rain sometimes see it as what shape?
questions.explanation: A rainbow is really a ring of light centred on the spot directly opposite the sun, and on the ground the earth simply blocks the bottom half. So there is no end of the rainbow, and no pot of gold either.

questions.question: Measured from its base on the sea floor to its summit, which Hawaiian volcano is taller than Mount Everest?
questions.explanation: Only about 4,200 metres of it stand above the sea, but the volcano rises more than 10,000 metres from the ocean floor, over a kilometre more than Everest.

questions.question: The Gen Z word 'rizz', meaning the power to charm or flirt, is a shortened form of which longer word?
questions.explanation: Rizz is taken from the middle of 'charisma', which is an unusual way to shorten a word. Oxford University Press named it its Word of the Year in 2023.

questions.question: The wireless technology that pairs your phone with your car is named after a tenth-century king of which country?
questions.explanation: Harald Bluetooth united Danish tribes, so engineers borrowed his name for a standard meant to unite devices, and the logo merges his runic initials.

questions.question: Na Slovensku im bežne hovoríme „čínske polievky“. V ktorej krajine však instantné rezance v skutočnosti vymysleli?
questions.explanation: Vymyslel ich Momofuku Ando, ktorý ich doma v kôlni vyvíjal pre firmu Nissin. Japonci ich v ankete dokonca vyhlásili za najlepší japonský vynález 20. storočia, pred karaoke aj walkmanom.

questions.question: Na ukazovateli paliva v aute je vedľa ikonky benzínovej pumpy malá šípka alebo trojuholníček. Čo vodičovi prezrádza?
questions.explanation: Šípka ukazuje, na ktorej strane auta je uzáver nádrže, takže aj v požičanom aute zastavíte k stojanu správne.

questions.question: Vianočný kapor, ktorý pláva vo vani, nemá v papuli ani jeden zub, a predsa potravu drví. Kde má kapor zuby?
questions.explanation: Kapor má takzvané hltanové zuby hlboko v hrdle a drví nimi potravu o tvrdú platničku. Preto vás pri chytaní do ruky nepohryzie.

questions.question: Turecký döner, grécky gyros aj arabská šaurma majú v pôvodnom jazyku takmer rovnaký význam. Čo znamenajú?
questions.explanation: Všetky tri názvy opisujú mäso, ktoré sa pomaly otáča na zvislom ražni pred ohňom. Keď si nabudúce v noci budete objednávať, v podstate si pýtate „to, čo sa točí“.

questions.question: Padel si väčšina ľudí spája so Španielskom. V ktorej krajine však tento šport v skutočnosti vznikol?
questions.explanation: Padel vymyslel v roku 1969 Enrique Corcuera na svojom pozemku v mexickom Acapulku. Do Španielska ho až neskôr priniesol jeho priateľ, princ Alfonso z Hohenlohe, a odtiaľ sa rozšíril do celej Európy.

questions.question: Slávna slovenská pieseň Hej, Slováci má rovnakú melódiu ako štátna hymna jednej našej susednej krajiny. Ktorej?
questions.explanation: Samo Tomášik napísal svoj text na melódiu poľskej piesne Mazurek Dąbrowského, ktorá sa neskôr stala poľskou hymnou. Ten istý nápev dlhé roky slúžil aj ako hymna Juhoslávie.

questions.question: In 1952, which world-famous physicist was offered the presidency of Israel and politely turned it down?

questions.question: Which burrowing Australian marsupial is the only animal known to produce cube-shaped droppings?

questions.question: Which is hotter: the surface of the Sun or a bolt of lightning?
questions.explanation: A lightning channel briefly reaches around 30,000 degrees Celsius, while the Sun's visible surface is only about 5,500 degrees. The Sun's core is far hotter, but its surface loses to a summer thunderstorm.

questions.question: The word 'galaxy' comes from an Ancient Greek word for an everyday drink. Which drink?
questions.explanation: The Greeks saw the pale band across the night sky as spilled milk, and called it 'galaxias' from 'gala', meaning milk. That is also why we still call our home galaxy the Milky Way.

questions.question: The word 'gym' comes from an ancient Greek word describing how athletes trained. What did that word mean?
questions.explanation: 'Gymnasium' comes from the Greek 'gymnos', meaning naked, because Greek athletes exercised in the nude. A dress code your local gym has firmly abandoned.

questions.question: High heels weren't invented for fashion. They began as practical footwear for men doing which activity?
questions.explanation: Persian cavalrymen wore heels so their feet would stay locked in the stirrups while they stood up to shoot arrows. European noblemen later copied the look, and only after that did heels become a women's fashion.

questions.question: France's longest land border isn't with any European country at all. Which country is it shared with?
questions.explanation: French Guiana in South America is a full part of France, and its border with Brazil runs about 730 kilometres, longer than France's border with Spain. So in a sense, Brazil is France's biggest neighbour.

questions.question: Climbers who reach the top of Mount Everest are standing on rock that formed at the bottom of what?
questions.explanation: The summit is limestone packed with fossils of tiny sea creatures, laid down on an ancient ocean floor. When India crashed into Asia, that seabed was pushed almost nine kilometres into the sky.

questions.question: Který chorvatský ostrov, kam se dá dojet autem po mostě, má název, jenž v češtině znamená část lidského těla?

questions.question: Patronem hasičů je svatý Florián. Jeho smrt má ale podle legendy ironický nádech. Jak zemřel?
questions.explanation: Římané ho svrhli do řeky Enns v dnešním Rakousku s kamenem uvázaným na krku. Ochránce před ohněm tak zahynul ve vodě.

questions.question: Olomoucké tvarůžky se navzdory názvu nevyrábějí v Olomouci. Ve kterém městě na Hané vznikají?
questions.explanation: Výroba se v Lošticích drží už od devatenáctého století a město má dokonce vlastní Muzeum Olomouckých tvarůžků.

questions.question: Která česká lidovka z tanečních zábav obletěla svět pod anglickým názvem Beer Barrel Polka?
questions.explanation: Vejvodovu polku hráli Glenn Miller i Andrews Sisters. Na konci druhé světové války ji zpívali vojáci po celém světě, aniž tušili, že pochází ze Zbraslavi.

questions.question: David Bowie's eyes famously looked like two different colours. What actually caused this illusion?
questions.explanation: His eyeball was scratched in a fight with a friend, leaving one pupil permanently dilated. Both eyes are actually the same colour.

questions.question: Which song from the animated film KPop Demon Hunters won Best Original Song at the 2026 Oscars?
questions.explanation: Performed in the film by the fictional group HUNTR/X, it had already spent weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2025 before adding an Oscar.

questions.question: Those little 'seeds' dotted over the outside of a strawberry aren't really seeds. Botanically, what is each one?
questions.explanation: Each speck is an achene, a complete little fruit with its own seed inside. The juicy red part we eat is just the swollen base of the flower.

questions.question: When a teenager replies to your joke with nothing but a skull emoji, what are they actually telling you?
questions.explanation: The skull is shorthand for 'I'm dead', as in dying of laughter. Many younger users now prefer it to the crying-laughing face, which they consider something their parents send.

questions.question: Since 1971, the United States has banned imports of traditional Scottish haggis because it contains which ingredient?
questions.explanation: American food rules forbid lungs in food for people, so authentic haggis with its sheep lung cannot be imported, though lung-free versions are made locally.

questions.question: Which 2025 vampire film set an all-time record at the 2026 Oscars with sixteen nominations?
questions.explanation: The bloodsoaked thriller out-nominated every film in Academy history and took home four statuettes on the night.

questions.question: Your ten fingernails don't all grow at the same speed. On a typical hand, which finger's nail grows the fastest?
questions.explanation: As a rough rule, the longer the finger, the faster its nail grows, so the middle finger leads and the little finger trails behind. Nails on your dominant hand also tend to grow a little faster than those on the other hand.

questions.question: Na palivoměru v autě je vedle ikonky benzínové pumpy malá šipka nebo trojúhelníček. Co vám ta šipka prozrazuje?
questions.explanation: Šipka ukazuje, na které straně auta je víčko nádrže, takže v půjčeném autě víte, ke kterému stojanu zajet. Klidně se teď podívejte na palubní desku.

questions.question: Když vezmete slunéčko sedmitečné do dlaně, často po něm zůstane žlutá, hořce páchnoucí kapička. Co to ve skutečnosti je?
questions.explanation: Vyděšené slunéčko vytlačí z kloubů na nohou vlastní krev, tedy hemolymfu. Je hořká a jedovatá, takže ptáci si ho příště rozmyslí.

questions.question: Slovo brambory vzniklo z názvu německé země, odkud k nám tyto hlízy kdysi přišly. Která země to byla?
questions.explanation: Brambory k nám přicházely z Braniborska, a tak se jim říkalo braniborky, z čehož časem vznikly brambory. Na Moravě se proto dodnes drží jiné názvy, třeba kobzole nebo zemáky.

questions.question: Pouťový perník dostal své jméno po koření, které se do těsta kdysi přidávalo. O jaké koření jde?
questions.explanation: Perník byl původně „pepřník“, protože se do medového těsta dával pepř. Slovo se časem obrousilo, ale ostrá stopa v něm zůstala.

questions.question: Kterou disciplínu běžel Emil Zátopek na olympiádě v Helsinkách roku 1952 poprvé v životě, a přesto v ní vyhrál?
questions.explanation: Ke zlatům na pět a deset kilometrů přidal i maratonské, a tento trojnásobný triumf na jedné olympiádě dodnes nikdo nezopakoval.

questions.question: Úhoř se nikdy nerozmnožuje v Evropě. Aby se vytřel, plave tisíce kilometrů přes Atlantik. Do kterého moře?
questions.explanation: Úhoři se třou v Sargasovém moři nedaleko Bermud a pak tam umírají. Jejich drobné larvy se nechají unášet proudy zpátky do Evropy, kde jejich rodiče žili.

questions.question: The 'lady' in the name ladybird, or ladybug, honours one specific woman. Who is she?
questions.explanation: Medieval farmers called it 'Our Lady's bird' and linked its red wings to Mary's cloak and its seven spots to her seven sorrows. German still calls it Marienkäfer, 'Mary's beetle'.

questions.question: The Italian surname Ferrari, now famous for sports cars, originally described a man's trade. Which trade?
questions.explanation: Ferrari comes from 'ferro', Italian for iron, so the world's most glamorous car brand is really Mr. Smith. It's the Italian cousin of Schmidt, Kovář and Kowalski.

questions.question: Which actor was working as a carpenter before being cast as Han Solo in the original Star Wars?
questions.explanation: Ford said he was quite surprised to be offered the part. His carpentry skills reportedly helped him land studio work where he was noticed.
